new_entities.name: Adolescent caffeine exposure
new_entities.description: Consumption of caffeine-containing beverages or products during adolescence, including coffee, energy drinks, and caffeinated soft drinks.

new_entities.name: Sleep and anxiety symptoms
new_entities.description: Combined sleep-quality, sleep-duration, and anxiety-related symptom outcomes.

edges.effect_quant: A 2023 meta-analysis found that caffeine reduced total sleep time by about 45 minutes and worsened several sleep-continuity measures, while adolescent observational data link higher energy-drink intake to shorter sleep and more emotional problems.
edges.population: adolescents and young people consuming caffeine, especially energy drinks and other high-caffeine beverages
edges.mechanism: Caffeine blocks adenosine signaling, delays sleep onset, reduces sleep continuity, and can amplify physiological arousal. In adolescents, those sleep disruptions can plausibly worsen anxiety, emotional lability, and related distress.
edges.summary: The clearest evidence is that caffeine worsens sleep, and adolescent observational data suggest that heavier caffeinated beverage use tracks with more emotional and behavioral problems. That is enough for a cautious harmful classification on the combined sleep-anxiety construct.
edges.caveats: Most adolescent evidence is observational and often uses energy-drink intake as the exposure, so confounding from broader lifestyle patterns is possible. The strongest causal evidence is for sleep disruption, while the anxiety component is more associative than experimentally proven.
